questions.title: Finding the Shift Constant from Sample Totals

parts.text: For $10$ values of $x$, the mean is $86.2$. Given that $\sum (x - a) = 362$, find the value of the constant $a$.

questions.title: Coded Mean from Given Mean and Shift

parts.text: For $24$ values of $x$, the mean is $52.5$. Given that $\sum (x - k) = 300$, find the value of $k$.

questions.title: Finding Sample Size from Coded and Raw Sums

parts.text:
For $n$ values of $x$, it is given that $\sum (x - 50) = 144$ and $\sum x = 944$.
Calculate the value of $n$.

questions.title: Direct Variance and Standard Deviation from Coded Totals

parts.text:
For $15$ values of $x$, it is given that $\sum (x - c) = 180$ and $\sum (x - c)^2 = 3300$, where $c$ is a constant.
Calculate the variance and standard deviation of $x$, giving the standard deviation correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Decoding the Coding Constant for Rental Prices

parts.text:
The rental prices, $x\text{ dollars}$, of $9$ apartments have a mean of $2205\text{ dollars}$.
Given that $\sum (x - c) = 1845$, find the value of the constant $c$.

questions.title: Finding an Additional Apartment Rental Price

parts.text:
The $9$ apartments from Drill 5 have a total rental price of $19845\text{ dollars}$. An additional apartment is rented, and the mean rental price of all $10$ apartments becomes $2120.50\text{ dollars}$.
Calculate the rental price of this additional apartment.

Five machine components have masses $x\text{ grams}$ of $502,\; 498,\; 505,\; 497,\; 503$.
Using the code $y = x - 500$, list the values of $y$ and calculate the mean of $x$.
Calculate $\sum y^2$, and hence find the standard deviation of $x$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

For a sample of $30$ values of $x$, it is given that $\sum (x - 50) = 450$.
Calculate the mean of $x$.
Given further that $\sum (x - 50)^2 = 8250$, calculate the variance and standard deviation of $x$, giving the standard deviation correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Coded Sum of Squares from Raw Summary

parts.text: For $12$ values of $x$, it is given that $\sum x = 186$. Find the value of $\sum (x - 10)$ and state the mean of $(x - 10)$.
Given that the standard deviation of $x$ is $4.5$, calculate the value of $\sum (x - 10)^2$.

questions.title: Recovering Shift Constant and Spread for 30 Exam Scores

parts.text:
For $30$ examination scores $x$, the mean is $50.5$. It is given that $\sum (x - k) = 315$ and $\sum (x - k)^2 = 4022$, where $k$ is an integer.
Find the value of $k$.
Calculate the variance and standard deviation of $x$, giving the standard deviation correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Apartment Rental Price Variance and Dispersion

parts.text:
The monthly rental prices, $x\text{ dollars}$, of $9$ apartments have a mean of $2205\text{ dollars}$.
It is given that $\sum (x - 2000) = 1845$ and $\sum (x - 2000)^2 = 477450$.
Calculate the variance and standard deviation of $x$.

A tenth apartment is added with rental price $1360\text{ dollars}$.
(i) State whether the mean rental price of all $10$ apartments will be greater than, equal to, or less than $2205\text{ dollars}$.
(ii) State whether the standard deviation of all $10$ apartments will be greater than, equal to, or less than $105\text{ dollars}$, giving a full reason in context.

questions.title: Combined Analysis of Two Linearly Coded Cohorts

parts.text:
Two groups of candidates took an aptitude test scored on a variable $x$. Both groups were coded using $y = x - 30$:
- Group $1$: $n_1 = 20$ candidates, $\sum(x - 30) = 439$
- Group $2$: $n_2 = 25$ candidates, $\sum(x - 30) = 470$

Calculate the combined mean $\bar{x}_{\text{comb}}$ of all $45$ candidates.

It is also given that $\sum (x - 30)^2 = 12405$ for Group $1$ and $\sum (x - 30)^2 = 11346$ for Group $2$.
Calculate the combined variance and the combined standard deviation of all $45$ candidates, giving the standard deviation correct to 3 significant figures.

For Group $1$, $\bar{x}_1 = 30 + \frac{439}{20} = 51.95$ and $\sigma_1 = \sqrt{\frac{12405}{20} - 21.95^2} = \sqrt{620.25 - 481.8025} = 11.8\text{ (3 s.f.)}$.
For Group $2$, $\bar{x}_2 = 30 + \frac{470}{25} = 48.80$ and $\sigma_2 = \sqrt{\frac{11346}{25} - 18.8^2} = \sqrt{453.84 - 353.44} = 10.0\text{ (3 s.f.)}$.
Compare the performance of Group $1$ and Group $2$ in context with respect to central score and consistency, and explain why the combined standard deviation ($10.9$) falls between $\sigma_2$ and $\sigma_1$.

questions.title: Comprehensive Topic Finale: Coded Distribution, Batch Merging, and Distribution Comparison

parts.text:
A horticultural study records the heights, $x\text{ cm}$, of $50$ seedlings grown under Condition $A$. Using the code $y = x - 40$, the recorded summaries are:
$$\sum (x - 40) = 350, \quad \sum (x - 40)^2 = 5450$$
Calculate the mean and standard deviation of the seedling heights under Condition $A$, giving the standard deviation correct to 3 significant figures.

A second batch of $10$ seedlings grown under Condition $B$ gives raw totals $\sum w = 520\text{ cm}$ and $\sum w^2 = 27800\text{ cm}^2$.
(i) Show that $\sum x^2 = 113450\text{ cm}^2$ for the $50$ seedlings under Condition $A$.
(ii) Calculate the combined mean and combined standard deviation of all $60$ seedlings, giving the standard deviation correct to 3 significant figures.

For Condition $B$, the $10$ seedlings have mean $\bar{w} = \frac{520}{10} = 52.0\text{ cm}$ and standard deviation $\sigma_B = \sqrt{\frac{27800}{10} - 52^2} = \sqrt{2780 - 2704} = \sqrt{76} \approx 8.72\text{ cm}$.
(i) Compare the growth of seedlings under Condition $A$ and Condition $B$ in terms of average height and variation.
(ii) Explain why the combined standard deviation ($8.13\text{ cm}$) of all $60$ seedlings exceeds the standard deviation of Condition $A$ alone ($7.75\text{ cm}$).
